Convert token containers to named documents

lexdiv_as_documents.Rd

Preserves document identity and token order while converting supported containers to the input used by lexdiv_metrics_batch().

Usage

lexdiv_as_documents(
  x,
  document_col = "document_id",
  token_col = "token"
)

Arguments

x

A named list of plain character token vectors, a data frame with one token per row, or a quanteda tokens object. Raw text is not tokenized.

document_col

The document-ID column in data-frame input.

token_col

The plain character token column in data-frame input.

Value

A plain named list of plain character vectors, preserving document and token order.

Details

lexdiv_as_documents() groups tidy token rows by first document appearance while preserving row order within each document. A quanteda tokens object is converted through its registered as.list() method, so ldfreq does not add a runtime dependency on quanteda. Raw text is not tokenized by this adapter. Each selected ID or token column must occur exactly once. Empty lists and zero-row token tables return the same named empty list, accepted by both lexdiv_metrics_batch() and lexdiv_profile_batch().

A one-token-per-row table has no row for a document with zero selected tokens. Retain the original document roster and represent those documents explicitly as named character() vectors before batch calculation. The adapter cannot recover IDs absent from the supplied table. For raw text, including empty texts, lexdiv_metrics_text_batch retains the declared IDs.

See also

lexdiv_metrics_batch, lexdiv_metrics_text_batch for raw text.

Examples

tokens <- data.frame(document_id = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  token = c("one", "two", "three", "three"))
documents <- lexdiv_as_documents(tokens)
lexdiv_metrics_batch(documents, metrics = "ttr")
#> <lexdiv_batch_results: 2 documents; 2 metric records; schema 0.1.0>
#>   document_id metric_id value status missing_reason N V below_quality_floor
#> 1           a       ttr   1.0     ok           <NA> 2 2               FALSE
#> 2           b       ttr   0.5     ok           <NA> 2 1               FALSE
